subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should arbitrary first-time plugin installs fail closed unless their source is ClawHub or mapped by OpenClaw-owned bundled/catalog metadata, while existing updates and selected guided flows remain exempt?
rationale: The patch can implement this policy safely, but choosing which executable sources and workflows OpenClaw treats as trusted is a security and compatibility decision that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve current trust model
options.body: Keep the exact source classification, interactive warning, noninteractive flag, chat restriction, and documented trusted-flow exemptions in this PR.

options.title: Narrow the policy
options.body: Gate fewer entry points or trust fewer source classes before landing, with focused compatibility coverage for the revised matrix.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Retain current install behavior until maintainers agree on a smaller executable-source policy change.

recommendation.title: Approve current trust model
recommendation.body: Keep the exact source classification, interactive warning, noninteractive flag, chat restriction, and documented trusted-flow exemptions in this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history shows the strongest ownership signal across both Crestodian and plugin-install behavior affected by this decision.
